D1_overlap.note: Propensity covariates: m24, state WNC share, state urban share, incumbency, statewide, region (district demographics unavailable). An archetype with no rows inside [0.05, 0.95] keeps only its structural (beta_L, beta_P) prediction and does not set the flag.

D2_ols_fe.rule_note: Compared only for archetypes with n >= 10 in the main sample (§3.8 cell minimum); smaller archetypes have no estimable dummy and are reported but not gated.

D3_freedman_lane.note: Residuals of the reduced OLS-FE model permuted within state; singleton states cannot permute.

D5_placebo.note: House seats on unchanged lines with a contested 2024 race where the 2026 D nominee was not the 2024 nominee/incumbent (text match on '2024 nominee'/'rematch'). Outcome house24 - pres24 (two-party). Controls: m24 spline, incumbency/opponent controls, region (no state FE: too few seats per state).

D6_close_primary_rd.note: Sign check only, never estimated into delta. Linear in primary margin with an m24 control; n is tiny.

D7_wave_compression.note: slopes per point of the state wave alpha_s (posterior mean), OLS-FE with CR2 SEs

V7_posterior_predictive.ES_slopes: not run: ES terms dropped (no district demographics)

V6_maine.scale: model scale = 50 x delta-logit (pts in an even seat); Maine is near even so it is ~ margin points

discrepancy.note: senate.json (NBC, 86% counted) has Jackson running +0.66 (total-vote) / -0.18 (two-party) ahead of Harris's 2024 Maine margin; the NYT nine-state table implies a -3.7-point shift (negative = toward R; 0.47*Male + 0.53*Female). Unresolved; both are preliminary. The NYT figure is a model estimate from early returns and its 2024 baseline may differ.

tau_c.note: r26 adds back the fitted personal-vote term (the model controls for it); oriented to the incumbent's party. Fallback tau_c=2 if < 40 incumbents or Cov <= 0.
